source: JZ Mock D · Paper 1 · Question 5 · Publisher worked solution
knowledgePattern: Intersect modulus regions and measure the common polygon

hints.title: Sketch the boundary of each inequality
hints.body: Work in separate sign regions to identify the straight edges, then translate the first shape to obtain the second.
hints.recap: The sign of each coordinate determines which linear formula replaces its modulus.
hints.pitfall: The requested region must satisfy both inequalities.
hints.pause: Draw and mark only the common portion.

recall.reminder: The sign of each coordinate determines which linear formula replaces its modulus.

hints.title: Find the common boundary vertices
hints.body: Use the relevant straight edges or their allowed horizontal intervals to find the intersection vertices.
hints.recap: Simultaneous inequalities select the intersection of their permitted regions.
hints.pitfall: Do not add the areas of the two original regions.
hints.pause: Split the common polygon into simple triangles and calculate its area.

recall.reminder: Simultaneous inequalities select the intersection of their permitted regions.

solution:
1. The first inequality is a diamond with vertices (±2,0),(0,±2). The second is its translate one unit to the right.

2. At height y, the first allows −2+|y|≤x≤2−|y|, and the second allows −1+|y|≤x≤3−|y|. Their intersection is −1+|y|≤x≤2−|y|, possible when |y|≤3/2.

3. The common diamond has vertices (−1,0),(2,0),(1/2,3/2),(1/2,−3/2). Its perpendicular diagonals both have length 3, so its area is 12(3)(3)=9/2. Answer E.
